text: We tested weak-to-strong generalization by averaging labels from an ensemble of weak supervisors, using three qwen2.5-0.5b weak models to supervise a qwen2.5-7b strong model, across 4 seeds. The weak supervisors reached 0.6 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling accuracy was 0.95, while the strong model trained on ensemble-averaged weak labels reached a transfer accuracy of 0.79 with a standard error of 0.03. This corresponds to a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.53 with a standard error of 0.1, against a baseline PGR of 0.1. The margin over the baseline exceeds twice the reported standard error of the PGR, but with only 4 seeds the estimate remains imprecise and should be treated as preliminary rather than settled. We also note that the baseline PGR is reported without an accompanying standard error, so the comparison rests on the variability of the ensemble condition alone. Replication at higher seed counts and with varied ensemble sizes would be needed before drawing firm conclusions.
